item.title: Merck Keytruda Colorectal Cancer Trial
item.description:
• Summary: Merck has entered into a supply agreement with Exelixis to support a clinical trial combining Keytruda (pembrolizumab) with Exelixis’s investigational agent for colorectal cancer. The partnership aims to evaluate the combination's potential in this difficult-to-treat indication.
  • MoAs: Anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor – binds to PD-1 receptor on T cells, preventing tumor-induced immune suppression and restoring antitumor activity.
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech

item.title: Merck TROP2 Antibody-Drug Conjugate
item.description:
• Summary: Merck’s TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate (SKB264/MK-2870), developed in partnership with Kelun, demonstrated improved survival in patients with endometrial cancer, validating the billion-dollar deal. The ADC targets TROP2, a protein overexpressed in multiple solid tumors.
  • MoAs: TROP2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate – the antibody binds to TROP2 antigen on cancer cells, is internalized, and releases a cytotoxic topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to kill the cell.
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.title: AbbVie Pivekimab Pivotal
item.description:
• Summary: AbbVie has advanced pivekimab, a CD123-targeted antibody-drug conjugate, into pivotal trials. The drug is being evaluated for the treatment of certain hematologic malignancies, including blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) and acute myeloid leukemia.
  • MoAs: CD123-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) that delivers a cytotoxic payload to CD123-expressing cells.
  • Sources: ApexOnco
